query.description: The day, YYYY-MM-DD in Brasília time; today when absent.

request.description:
The merchant's day at a glance (payments:read, or the merchant's own app session)

Sales, gross, fees and net captured on a Brasília day, split by payment method and by hour, against the same weekday a week before (up to the same time of day for today), the charges still waiting, and the day's latest payments.

item.name: The merchant's sales by day over a period, against the period before (payments:read, or the merchant's own app session)

request.description:
The merchant's sales by day over a period, against the period before (payments:read, or the merchant's own app session)

From one Brasília day to another, both included, at most 92 days; the last 30 days
ending today by default. Each day is listed, days without sales included. The previous
period is as long and ends the day before; when the period ends today the previous one
ends at the same time of day, so the comparison is fair.

item.name: Register a terminal (DE 41) and bind its attested mTLS certificate

request.description:
Register a terminal (DE 41) and bind its attested mTLS certificate

Binds a terminal ID to a merchant. certificate_sha256 is the fingerprint of the terminal's
mutual-TLS certificate, issued by the terminal PKI after device attestation (docs/05 §2.4);
requests on the terminal host are authenticated by that certificate. Sending a CSR for the
platform to sign returns 501 until the terminal PKI is enabled.

item.name: Revoke a terminal (lost, stolen or decommissioned device)

request.description:
Revoke a terminal (lost, stolen or decommissioned device)

The terminal's certificate stops authenticating and its terminal ID takes no further
authorizations. Revocation is permanent and recorded in the audit trail; register a new
terminal for a replacement device. Sends terminal.revoked.

request.description:
Card-present authorization from an MPoC terminal (terminal host, CDE)

An iPhone attested with App Attest sends App-Attest-Assertion: the assertion its attested key makes over SHA-256 of this exact request body (DCAppAttestService generateAssertion). Without it, with another key, over another body or with a counter already used, the request is refused with 403 assertion-invalid before it reaches the card network.

item.name: Sandbox only. The customer pays a Pix charge

request.description:
Sandbox only. The customer pays a Pix charge

The PSP simulator pays the charge as a bank app would; its webhook then captures the
payment, and the partner's webhooks follow. The answer waits up to five seconds for the
capture. The charge must be a Pix payment intent confirmed and waiting (requires_action).

item.name: terminals
Upload the device's signed, hash-chained journal entries (kind 7714)

request.description:
Upload the device's signed, hash-chained journal entries (kind 7714)

App sessions only; every entry must be signed by the session's device key and name the
merchant's root key. Entries are stored in seq order; re-sent entries count as duplicates.
The answer is the HTTPS form of the 27711 / 27712 reconciliation (docs/03 §9): `missing`
lists the seq ranges the platform lacks, and a second entry at a stored seq, or a prev that
is not the entry before it, is kept as proof of a fork and freezes the device's terminal.

Resolve a review

item.name: Stop sending to an endpoint, for good

request.description:
Stop sending to an endpoint, for good

No new events are queued for it and its pending deliveries are abandoned. It stays
listed, disabled, with its history; replaying to it answers 409, so create a new
endpoint and replay there. Calling it again answers the same. Recorded in the audit trail.

item.name: Replay deliveries for a time range

request.description:
Replay deliveries for a time range

Schedules every delivery of the endpoint created in [since, until) again, delivered or
not, with its original webhook-id so the receiver can deduplicate. At most the last 30
days and 10 000 deliveries per call.

item.name: Issue a new signing secret (webhooks:write)

request.description:
Issue a new signing secret (webhooks:write)

The new secret is returned once. The old one keeps signing beside it for overlap_hours (default 24, at most 168): deliveries in that window carry both signatures, so the receiver can switch when its deploy lands. A leaked secret is rotated with 0.

item.name: Send crypto the merchant holds to an outside address (payouts:write)

request.description:
Send crypto the merchant holds to an outside address (payouts:write)

Final once sent. The address is checked against the network's format and screened against sanctions lists before anything moves: a listed address is refused with 403 address_refused, and a screening that cannot be completed with 503 (nothing is sent either way; every screening is recorded). The network fee is taken from the holding. The travel rule goes first (docs/09 §6.6): to another provider (destination_type exchange, beneficiary_vasp required) the receiving provider must accept the IVMS101 data before anything moves (422 travel_rule_rejected, or 503 without an answer); to a self-hosted wallet the request records the owner's declaration.

item.name: Release, block or close a case (compliance:write)

request.description:
Release, block or close a case (compliance:write)

release: the hold is undone and a payment that waited settles. block: the coins stay frozen in liability.compliance_hold and the payment is canceled; operations reports it (runbook §4.12). close: a review, nothing was held. The note is required and kept with who decided; a case already decided answers 409.

item.name: Retrieve a travel-rule message with its payload (travel_rule:read)

request.description:
Retrieve a travel-rule message with its payload (travel_rule:read)

The IVMS101 payload names people and their documents: it is stored sealed and read only with travel_rule:read, which a "*" key does not include. A redacted message (past the record-keeping period) has redacted_at and no payload.

item.name: A message another provider sent (the travel-rule adapter only)

request.description:
A message another provider sent (the travel-rule adapter only)

Signed with the adapter's shared secret in the webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature headers (HMAC-SHA256, as the platform's own webhooks). The answer is the platform's to the sender; the same reference twice answers the first result.
